2611.26806.image_caption: Figure 1 : MedicalRSI Outperforms Existing Methods and Keeps Improving over Training. Left : tasks solved on MedAgentBench with Qwen3.5-9B , with the methods grouped by what they change: the harness only (context-level: an RL-trained improver, GRASP, or a frontier LLM writing the harness), the model only (weight-level), or neither (a frontier LLM solving the tasks itself, or the Base Agent , whose score the dashed line marks). Right : MedicalRSI keeps improving over the training rounds. It also improves faster: after two rounds, it already passes the final scores of the two strongest trained baselines.

2611.26912.image_caption: Fig. 1: Architecture of ZhuLong-SE, adapted from the ZhuLong execution framework [ 1 ] . Blue-highlighted blocks denote components added or enhanced in this work. Unhighlighted blocks show the shared execution workflow.

2611.27110.image_caption: Figure 1 : Motivation of RemoteEvolver. Top : Remote sensing agents encounter unbridgeable capability gaps when required specialized tools are missing from their predefined toolsets. Bottom : Comparison of existing remote sensing agent evolution paradigms.

2611.27285.image_caption: Figure 1 : Execution workflows of existing IR agents and our SIR-Agent. (a) Explicit-memory methods retrieve external restoration knowledge for tool-chain generation. (b) Implicit-memory methods encode restoration knowledge into model parameters via training. (c) The SIR-Agent progressively loads skills with a frozen MLLM. Chain feedback enables skill revision, while RSI optimizes revision rules.

2611.27646.image_caption: Figure 1: Motivation for model-conditioned harness adaptation. (a) A fixed harness is shared across planner–observer stacks despite their different failure patterns; exposing all available capabilities does not necessarily resolve this mismatch. (b) Starting from the same lightweight harness, MoHA adapts planner-facing modules, observer assignments, and execution configurations to each hosted stack.

2611.27689.image_caption: Figure 1: Framework of Embodied-Harness. (a) The Actor performs task execution through a perception–action loop guided by the execution harness. (b) Hierarchical memory maintains short-term execution context and long-term experience across attempts and tasks. (c) The Reflector analyzes execution evidence and experience to diagnose failures and identify improvements. (d) Recursive harness self-improvement generates guidance and refines operational knowledge to improve subsequent execution without updating model parameters.

2611.27780.image_caption: Figure 1 : Fixed pool and static world growth (top) vs. Search-RSI (bottom) on an MMSearch question. A fixed pool never asks the second hop; static growth asks it without its supporting fact, so a correct search is penalized. Search-RSI injects the support of the task, and the improved policy π t + 1 \pi_{t+1} diagnoses, admits, and demonstrates the tasks of the next round.

2611.27797.image_caption: Fig. 1: Overview of EvoTER. Left: Embodied tool-use agent. Skills guide the selection and composition of heterogeneous tools through a unified interface, while execution feedback closes the decision loop. Right: Experience-driven skill evolution. Explorer collects execution trajectories; Diagnoser extracts and revises skills, with privileged simulator information available only after exploration stagnates; Validator evaluates candidate and current libraries using ordinary observations and tools, retains candidates improving aggregate validation success, and returns rejected candidates to Diagnoser for revision.

2611.26853.image_caption: Figure 3 : Episodes from the same initial state without and with LoCo-WAM. Frames every 2 s. The first decision at which the two runs differ and the frame at which LoCo-WAM completes the task are outlined. Long-WAM with 4.8 s of history on RoboCasa GR-1.

2611.27095.image_note: Genuine source Table 1 used as the paper visual. This is an algorithm/table crop rather than a numbered figure.

2611.27156.image_caption: Figure 1 . Cross-actor detection performance ( F 1 F_{1} ) of BERT, xLSTM, their fusion (BERT+xLSTM), and IO-AI. Rows indicate training actors, columns indicate test actors, and diagonal cells show in-domain performance.

2611.27216.image_caption: Figure 2: Even recently released models are susceptible. Each stem is one model’s change in safe rate after one correct precedent, placed at its release date. A drop of more than 5 points is an unacceptable safety compromise.

2611.27219.image_caption: Figure 1 : From explicit to parametric memory in VLN. NavTTT replaces explicit or token-based history with episode-specific parametric memory stored in fast weights.

2611.27381.image_caption: Figure 1 : Overview of VMSA. (a) Structured video memory comprises three levels: segment captions preserving local details, entity events consolidating observations of continuing activities, and entity-aware episodes connecting related episodes across distant time points. (b) Memory skills are induced from successful source trajectories. Coverage assessment determines whether each procedure is already covered, requires skill refinement, or requires a new skill. The skill libraries are updated accordingly and periodically consolidated to reduce redundancy while preserving procedural knowledge. (c) At inference time, the video agent receives the target query, retrieved memory skills, and entity-aware episode memory as input context. The agent then gathers and verifies evidence through tool calls to generate its answer.

2611.26747.image_caption: Figure 1: The SkillPrivus Privacy Card , the output of a static audit, showing ( what it says it does ) vs ( what the code actually does ) for a real apple-health skill collected from a public marketplace.

2611.26910.image_caption: Figure 1: Types of evidence an agent can ground knowledge in: observation (by eye or through an instrument), testimony (dialogue or writing, shown as on-screen text), and interaction, the result of the agent’s own action ( Gopnik et al., 2004 ; Harris and Koenig, 2006 ) . Screenshots from Outer Wilds, © Mobius Digital.

2611.27425.image_caption: Figure 1 : One-shot backdoor injection into ShieldGemma 2 using WSP. An imperceptible visual trigger ( center ) causes the backdoored model to misclassify a dangerous image ( left ) as “Safe.” The trigger is amplified 28 × 28\times for better visualization.
